references.text: God commands Noah to bring two of every living creature into the ark, male and female, to keep them alive – this is the original instruction that Noah carries out in Gen 7:9.
Further instructions to take seven pairs of clean animals and birds, along with one pair of unclean animals, elaborating on the details of entering the ark in pairs.
Noah did everything just as the Lord had commanded him, which directly corresponds to the conclusion in Gen 7:9: 'just as God had commanded Noah'.
Describes how the animals entered the ark two by two from all flesh, male and female, just as God had commanded – a direct parallel and repetition of Gen 7:9.
Uses the same Hebrew expression זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה (male and female) regarding the creation of humanity, as in Gen 7:9 concerning animal pairs.
By faith Noah built the ark to save his household, just as God had spoken – Noah's obedience to God's command is the central theme linking this to Gen 7:9.
A direct continuation of the same event confirming that the animals came two by two just as God had commanded.
The New Testament's allusion to the flood as an example of judgment upon a complacent generation.
A concrete example of the total obedience described as Noah's defining characteristic in Gen 6:22.
Logical and narrative connection between God's command to Noah and the animals' subsequent entry.
The New Testament's use of the flood as a theological example of judgment upon a complacent world.
Complementary events showing the completeness of God's plan of salvation from entry to exit.
